proposals.hypothesis: D07 (2,6-dichloro-BQ) is the best-f parent (f=1.24, bind -25.8, no detachment) but its O2 margin is only 0.097. Ring halogenation raised the margin: D08 (F4) 0.178, D14 (Cl4) 0.346, D11 (Br4) 0.462. Heavier halogens cost binding, though (f fell from 1.24 to 0.72 with Cl4 and to 0.28 with Br4), so I add one Br and one F instead of filling the ring with a single heavy halogen. Br should lift the margin above 0.15. F is small and kept strong CO2 binding in D08 (bind -24.3, f=1.03), so it should limit the binding loss. K084 and K029 report CO2 adducts for tetrafluoro-BQ and chloranil, and K058 and K055 show that halogenated BQs stay reducible. I avoided CN (D03, D06, D10 all detached CO2) and NH2/OH (D01, D02, D04, D05 lowered f). This is a promoted-direction test: a mixed F/Cl/Br benzoquinone should combine D07's binding with a margin of at least 0.15. Risk: f may still stay below 2, since no reference reached it, and the margin gain may not offset the binding loss seen from D07 to D14 and D11. DFT will decide.
